text:
Marathon Petroleum's stock fell 7.4% today after climbing $13 on October 26th on diplomatic hopes, reversing sharply as geopolitical uncertainty persisted. The driver appears to be conflicting signals: while Houthi attacks on Saudi refineries initially pushed oil prices higher on October 28th (signaling tighter supply that benefits refiners), Trump's comments the same day about prolonging the Iran conflict seem to have spooked investors about sustained instability rather than a quick resolution. Oil prices remain elevated at $107.89 domestically and $115.22 globally, but the stock's sharp reversal suggests traders are pricing in risk rather than opportunity from this volatility.

The broader picture adds weight to the selloff: refineries are running at 93.4% capacity with healthy diesel and gasoline inventories, meaning the company is already operating near full throttle and may have limited upside from higher crude prices. In this environment, geopolitical noise that could disrupt supply chains or demand without substantially boosting margins—especially when the Trump administration is also considering flooding the market with Russian diesel—may be hitting the stock's valuation more than supporting it.
